senses.en: change from a liquid to a thickened or solid state

examples.text: In cheese making, milk coagulates into curds that become cheese.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coāgulō('응고시키다')에서 왔고, cōgō(함께 몰아넣다)와 관련됩니다. 흩어진 것을 한데 몰아 굳히는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To join into a mass or whole.

examples.text: The droplets coalesced into a puddle.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coalēscō에서 왔고, co-(함께)와 alēscō(자라다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 함께 자라 하나가 된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To make a minimal effort; to continue to do something in a routine way, without initiative or effort.

examples.text: After winning the early rounds, the team coasted through the rest of the season without much effort.

senses.en: move effortlessly; by force of gravity

examples.text: The cyclist stopped pedaling and coasted down the long hill toward the village.

origin.ko: 라틴어 costa('갈비뼈, 옆구리')에서 왔고, 고대 프랑스어에서 '옆, 해안'이라는 뜻이 되었습니다. 동사는 해안을 따라 가다에서 파생됩니다.

senses.en: influence or urge by gentle urging, caressing, or flattering

examples.text: He coaxed the horse gently into the trailer.

origin.ko: 1586년 은어 'make a coax of'(바보 취급하다)에서 시작됐고 기원은 불분명합니다.

senses.en: A conclusion (of a statement or event, for example), final portion, tail end.

examples.text: The memoir ends with a brief coda reflecting on how the town has changed since.

senses.en: the closing section of a musical composition

examples.text: The symphony builds to a thundering coda that leaves the audience breathless.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 coda('꼬리')에서 왔고 라틴어 cauda와 같은 어원입니다. 곡의 꼬리 부분이 '끝맺음'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: treat with excessive indulgence

examples.text: Critics argue that universities coddle students instead of preparing them for professional criticism.

origin.ko: 아마 caudle에서 왔을 것으로 추정되며, 확실하지는 않습니다.

senses.en: An addition or supplement that explains, modifies, or revokes a will or part of one.

examples.text: She added a codicil to her will leaving the family cottage to her nephew.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōdicillus에서 왔고, cōdex(책)의 지소형입니다. 유언장에 덧붙이는 '작은 서판'입니다.

senses.en: Actual or threatened force for the purpose of compelling action by another person; the act of coercing.

examples.text: The confession was thrown out because the court found it had been obtained through coercion.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coërcitiō에서 왔고, coërceō는 co-와 arceō(가두다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 울타리에 가두듯 억누르는 힘입니다.

senses.en: A supply or store of money, often belonging to an organization.

examples.text: The new tax was intended to replenish the depleted coffers of the municipal government.

senses.en: a chest especially for storing valuables

examples.text: The merchant locked the gold coins in an iron coffer beneath his bed.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 cofre('상자')에서 왔고, 그리스어 kophinos(바구니)까지 거슬러 갑니다. coffin과 같은 어원입니다.

senses.en: powerfully persuasive

examples.text: The senator presented a cogent argument that swayed several undecided colleagues.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōgēns에서 왔고, cōgō('함께 몰아붙이다, 강제하다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 상대를 몰아붙이는 설득력입니다.

senses.en: To meditate, to ponder, to think deeply.

examples.text: He cogitated for weeks before deciding whether to leave academia for industry.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōgitō('생각하다')에서 왔고 1570년에 처음 기록됩니다.

senses.en: having the same ancestral language

examples.text: cognate languages

senses.en: a word is cognate with another if both derive from the same word in an ancestral language

examples.text: The English word night and the German word Nacht are cognates descended from a common ancestor.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cognātus('혈연으로 이어진')에서 왔고, co-(함께)와 gnātus(태어난)가 합쳐졌습니다. 같은 뿌리에서 난 말입니다.

senses.en: have internal elements or parts logically connected so that aesthetic consistency results

examples.text: The essay's scattered observations fail to cohere into a persuasive overall argument.

senses.en: come or be in close contact with; stick or hold together and resist separation

examples.text: Wet sand coheres far better than dry sand, which is why sandcastles need water.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cohaereō('함께 달라붙다, 일관되다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: cohering or tending to cohere; well integrated

examples.text: a team welded into a cohesive unit

origin.ko: 라틴어 cohaesus(cohaereō의 과거분사)에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 서로 달라붙어 결속된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An accomplice; abettor; associate.

examples.text: He was able to plea down his sentence by revealing the names of three of his cohorts, as well as the source of the information.

senses.en: a group of people having approximately the same age

examples.text: Researchers followed a cohort of children born in 1990 to study long-term health outcomes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cohors에서 왔고 court와 같은 어원입니다. 로마 군대의 한 부대에서 '동료 무리'로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: the arrangement of the hair (especially a woman's hair)

examples.text: Her elaborate coiffure required nearly two hours of work by a team of stylists.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 coiffure를 그대로 빌려 온 말입니다.

senses.en: make up a word or phrase

examples.text: The economist coined the term gig economy to describe short-term, freelance work arrangements.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 coigne('쐐기, 주화 찍는 틀')에서 왔고 라틴어 cuneus(쐐기)가 뿌리입니다. 틀로 찍어 새로 만든다는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: work together on a common enterprise or project

examples.text: Physicists and biologists increasingly collaborate on problems that span both disciplines.

senses.en: cooperate as a traitor

examples.text: After the war, officials who had collaborated with the occupiers were put on trial.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 collabōrāre('함께 일하다')에서 왔고 collaborator에서 거꾸로 만들어진 말입니다.

senses.en: careful examination and comparison to note points of disagreement

examples.text: The editor's collation of the three manuscripts revealed dozens of discrepancies in the text.

senses.en: a light informal meal

examples.text: A cold collation of bread, cheese, and fruit was laid out for the guests.

origin.ko: 라틴어 collatiō에서 왔고 cōnferō('함께 가져오다')의 분사 어간이 뿌리입니다. 가져와 나란히 비교한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: act in unison or agreement and in secret towards a deceitful or illegal purpose

examples.text: Regulators accused the airlines of colluding to keep ticket prices artificially high.

origin.ko: 라틴어 collūdere에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 lūdere(놀다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 짜고 함께 놀아난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: agreement on a secret plot

examples.text: The inquiry found evidence of collusion between the contractors to rig the bidding process.

origin.ko: 라틴어 collusio('공모 행위')에서 온 고대 프랑스어 collusion에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe

examples.text: The project proved a colossal waste of public money and years of planning.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 colossal에서 왔고, 라틴어 colossus를 거쳐 그리스어 kolossos('거대한 조각상')가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: a state or atmosphere of harmony or mutual civility and respect

examples.text: Despite sharp disagreements, the two parties preserved a measure of comity in the chamber.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōmitās(공손함, 호의)에서 왔고 후기 중세 영어 comite로 들어왔습니다.

senses.en: take the first step or steps in carrying out an action

examples.text: The speeches commenced three days of workshops, seminars, and cultural activities.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 comencer에서 왔고, 속라틴어 *cominitiāre(com- + initiō)가 뿌리입니다. initiate와 같은 계통입니다.

senses.en: worthy of high praise

examples.text: The volunteers showed commendable restraint while working through the long, exhausting night.

origin.ko: 라틴어 commendabilis에서 왔고, commendare는 manus(손)와 dare(주다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 손에 맡길 만큼 믿음직하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: corresponding in size or degree or extent

examples.text: The rewards will be commensurate with the efforts made.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 commēnsūrātus에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 mēnsūrō(재다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 같은 척도로 재서 맞는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: to feel or express sympathy or compassion

examples.text: Colleagues gathered to commiserate with her after the grant proposal was rejected.

origin.ko: 라틴어 commiseror에서 왔고, '함께 불쌍히 여기다'는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A body or group of people, officially tasked with carrying out a particular function.

examples.text: the European Commission

senses.en: A fee charged by an agent or broker for carrying out a transaction.

examples.text: a reseller's commission

senses.en: To place an order for (often a piece of art).

examples.text: The museum commissioned a mural from a local artist to mark its centennial.

origin.ko: 라틴어 commissiō('함께 보냄, 위임')에서 왔고, committō에 -tiō가 붙었습니다. 어떤 일을 맡겨 보낸 사람들의 모임이 '위원회'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: give entirely to a specific person, activity, or cause

examples.text: She committed herself to the work of God

senses.en: To do (something bad); to perpetrate, as a crime, sin, or fault.

examples.text: to commit murder

senses.en: To give in trust; to put into charge or keeping; to entrust; to consign; used with to or formerly unto.

examples.text: The students were told to commit the formulas to memory before the exam.

origin.ko: 라틴어 committō('함께 두다, 맡기다')에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 mittō(보내다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 자신을 어떤 일에 내맡긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: force somebody to do something

examples.text: New regulations compel companies to disclose the chemicals used in their products.

senses.en: necessitate or exact

examples.text: The severe water shortage compels strict conservation measures across the region.

origin.ko: 라틴어 compellere에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 pellere(몰다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 가축을 한데 몰듯 강제한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: tending to persuade by forcefulness of argument

examples.text: He made a compelling argument.

senses.en: very interesting; able to capture and hold one's attention

examples.text: The novel was so compelling that I couldn't put it down.

origin.ko: compel(강요하다)에 -ing가 붙은 말입니다. 마음을 몰아붙이는 설득력입니다.

senses.en: a concise but comprehensive summary of a larger work

examples.text: The handbook serves as a compendium of the field's major findings over the past century.

senses.en: a publication containing a variety of works

examples.text: The compendium gathers essays, poems, and letters from dozens of nineteenth-century writers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 compendium('함께 달아 본 것, 절약, 축약')에서 왔습니다. 많은 내용을 달아 추려 낸 요약본입니다.

senses.en: adequate, but not outstanding or exceptional

examples.text: The orchestra gave a competent but uninspired performance of the familiar symphony.

senses.en: properly or sufficiently qualified or capable or efficient

examples.text: a competent typist

origin.ko: 라틴어 competens에서 왔고, competō('들어맞다, 감당할 수 있다')에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: contented to a fault with oneself or one's actions

examples.text: The company grew complacent after years of market dominance and ignored emerging competitors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 complacēns('매우 기쁘게 하는')에서 왔고, com-과 placēre(기쁘게 하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 스스로 만족해 안주한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: showing a cheerful willingness to do favors for others

examples.text: The complaisant host agreed to every request his guests made, however inconvenient.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 complaisant('기꺼이 비위를 맞추는')에서 왔고, 라틴어 complacēre(잘 기쁘게 하다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: acting as or providing a complement (something that completes the whole)

examples.text: The two business partners had complementary abilities: one had excellent people skills, while the other had a head for figures.

origin.ko: complement(보충)에 -ary가 붙은 말입니다. complimentary와 같은 어원에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: inclined to comply

examples.text: The suspect was compliant when arrested.

senses.en: involved with others in an activity that is unlawful or morally wrong

examples.text: Officials who looked the other way were seen as complicit in the fraud.

origin.ko: complicity에서 거꾸로 만들어진 말이며, explicit 같은 단어의 영향을 받았다고 봅니다.

senses.en: act in accordance with someone's rules, commands, or wishes

examples.text: He complied with my instructions

origin.ko: 라틴어 complēre('가득 채우다, 이행하다')에서 왔습니다. 요구를 빈틈없이 채워 따른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To be in agreement (with); to be of an accord.

examples.text: The new rules did not seem to comport with the spirit of the club.

senses.en: To behave (in a given manner).

examples.text: She comported herself with grace.

origin.ko: 라틴어 comportare('함께 가져오다')에서 왔습니다. 함께 가져와 맞춘다는 뜻에서 '부합하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: make more intense, stronger, or more marked

examples.text: The delay in sending aid only compounded the suffering of the flood victims.

senses.en: a whole formed by a union of two or more elements or parts

examples.text: The final design was a compound of several earlier architectural styles.

origin.ko: 라틴어 componō('함께 놓다')에서 온 중세 프랑스어 componre에서 왔습니다. 요소를 겹쳐 쌓아 더 심하게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: including all or everything

examples.text: a comprehensive history of the revolution

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 comprehēnsīvus에서 왔고 comprehendō(움켜쥐다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 모두 한 번에 움켜쥐는 포괄성입니다.

senses.en: expose or make liable to danger, suspicion, or disrepute

examples.text: The leak of classified files compromised the integrity of the entire investigation.

senses.en: an accommodation in which both sides make concessions

examples.text: After weeks of talks, the negotiators reached a compromise that neither side found ideal.

origin.ko: 라틴어 compromittere('함께 약속하다')에서 왔고, 원래는 중재 결정을 따르겠다는 상호 약속이었습니다. 약속에 얽매여 위태로워진다는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: To admit or agree to be true; to acknowledge

examples.text: The author concedes that her sample size was small but insists the trend is real.

senses.en: acknowledge defeat

examples.text: The candidate conceded after enough votes had come in to show that he would lose

origin.ko: 라틴어 concēdō('양보하다')에서 왔고, con-(완전히)과 cēdō(물러나다)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: an elaborate poetic image or a far-fetched comparison of very dissimilar things

examples.text: Donne's famous conceit compares two separated lovers to the legs of a drawing compass.

senses.en: feelings of excessive pride

examples.text: His conceit was so great that he never asked anyone for advice.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 conceyte에서 왔고 conceyven(생각해 내다)에서 만들어졌습니다. concept와 같은 어원으로, 머릿속에 붙든 기발한 생각입니다.

senses.en: an abstract or general idea inferred or derived from specific instances

examples.text: The concept of justice has been debated by philosophers for more than two thousand years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conceptus('생각, 잉태')에서 왔고 concipiō(받아들이다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 머릿속에 붙잡아 품은 생각입니다.

senses.en: be relevant to

examples.text: The new policy concerns only those employees hired after the merger.

senses.en: an anxious feeling

examples.text: Doctors expressed concern about the rapid spread of the infection in rural areas.

origin.ko: 라틴어 concernō('함께 체로 치다, 섞다')에서 왔고 con-과 cernō(가려내다)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of

examples.text: The mayor tried to conciliate angry residents by promising to reopen the community center.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conciliō('하나로 합치다')에서 왔고 concilium(회의, 모임)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: intended to placate

examples.text: The minister struck a conciliatory tone in her address to the striking workers.

senses.en: forming an end or termination; especially putting an end to doubt or question

examples.text: conclusive evidence

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 conclusivus에서 왔고, concludere(닫아 끝내다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 문을 닫아 의문을 끝낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: occurring with or following as a consequence

examples.text: Rapid urban growth brings concomitant problems of congestion and pollution.

origin.ko: 라틴어 concomitor('함께 동행하다')에서 왔고, comes(동반자)가 뿌리입니다. 곁에 붙어 같이 따라오는 것입니다.

senses.en: be in accord; be in agreement

examples.text: I do not concur that this is the best way forward.

senses.en: happen simultaneously

examples.text: The drought and the economic downturn concurred, making the crisis far harder to manage.

origin.ko: 라틴어 concurro('함께 달리다, 의견이 일치하다')에서 왔습니다. 같은 방향으로 달려 만난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: excuse, overlook, or make allowances for; be lenient with

examples.text: The school does not condone cheating under any circumstances.

origin.ko: 라틴어 condōnāre('용서하다')를 학술적으로 빌려 온 말입니다. 잘못을 선물처럼 넘겨 준다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: tending to bring about; being partly responsible for

examples.text: A small, dark kitchen is not conducive to elaborate cooking.

origin.ko: 라틴어 condūcere('함께 이끌다')에서 온 conduce에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 좋은 결과로 이끈다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: manner of acting or controlling yourself

examples.text: The committee praised the soldiers for their exemplary conduct under extreme pressure.

senses.en: direct the course of; manage or control

examples.text: The team conducted a rigorous survey of more than two thousand households.

senses.en: transmit or serve as the medium for transmission

examples.text: Copper conducts electricity far more efficiently than most other common metals.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 conductus('호위, 인도')에서 왔고, condūcō(함께 이끌다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 이끌린 대로 하는 행동이 '품행'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To grant as a possession; to bestow.

examples.text: The college has conferred an honorary degree upon the visiting Prime Minister.

senses.en: have a conference in order to talk something over

examples.text: We conferred about a plan of action

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnferō('함께 가져오다')에서 왔습니다. 모아서 건네준다는 뜻에서 '수여하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a very intense and uncontrolled fire

examples.text: A single spark from the warehouse ignited a conflagration that consumed the entire block.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnflagrātiō('완전히 불탐')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To fail to properly distinguish or keep separate (things); to mistakenly treat (them) as equivalent.

examples.text: Critics warn against conflating correlation with causation when interpreting the survey results.

senses.en: mix together different elements

examples.text: The film conflates two historical figures into a single character.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnflō('함께 불다, 녹여 합치다')에서 왔습니다. 풀무로 불어 두 쇳덩이를 하나로 녹여 붙이는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: A convergence or combination of forces, people, or things.

examples.text: The confluence of our skills resulted in a successful home renovation project.

senses.en: a place where things merge or flow together (especially rivers)

examples.text: Pittsburgh is located at the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 cōnfluentia('함께 흐름')에서 왔습니다. 강물이 합쳐지는 모습입니다.

senses.en: be confusing or perplexing to; cause to be unable to think clearly

examples.text: The unexpected results confounded researchers, who had predicted the opposite outcome.

senses.en: To defeat, to frustrate, to thwart.

examples.text: The champion confounded expectations by winning the title with a seriously injured shoulder.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnfundō('함께 붓다, 뒤섞다')에서 왔습니다. 모두 섞어 뒤죽박죽 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To change from a liquid to solid state, perhaps due to cold; called to freeze in nontechnical usage.

examples.text: The gravy congealed on the plate while the guests lingered over their conversation.

senses.en: To make rigid or immobile.

examples.text: We must act before opposition to our plans congeals.

origin.ko: 라틴어 congelare에서 왔고 프랑스어를 거쳤습니다. 완전히 얼어 굳는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Friendly or sociable.

examples.text: The congenial bartender makes the Hog’s Head an inviting place to hang out during the weekends.

senses.en: suitable to your needs

examples.text: The quiet library provided a congenial atmosphere for the long hours of reading.

origin.ko: con-(함께)에 genial(타고난 기질의)이 붙은 말입니다. 기질이 서로 맞는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: based primarily on surmise rather than adequate evidence

examples.text: Any account of the city's earliest years remains largely conjectural because few records survive.

senses.en: of or relating to marriage or to the relationship between a wife and husband

examples.text: The prison eventually allowed conjugal visits for inmates serving long sentences.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coniugālis에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 iugum(멍에)이 합쳐졌습니다. 한 멍에를 함께 멘 부부의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: summon into action or bring into existence, often as if by magic

examples.text: The smell of fresh bread conjured memories of her grandmother's kitchen.

senses.en: ask for or request earnestly

examples.text: The old priest conjured the villagers to forgive one another before the winter began.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coniūrō('함께 맹세하다, 공모하다')에서 왔습니다. 주문으로 영혼을 불러내는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: acting together in secret toward a fraudulent or illegal end

examples.text: The conniving advisor quietly steered the young king toward decisions that benefited only himself.

senses.en: an expert able to appreciate a field; especially in the fine arts

examples.text: As a connoisseur of early jazz, he owned thousands of rare recordings.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 connoisseur에서 왔고 connoître('알다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 1700년대 초에 영어로 들어왔습니다.

senses.en: an idea that is implied or suggested

examples.text: The word cheap carries a negative connotation that thrifty does not.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 connotātiō에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 notō(표시하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 본뜻 옆에 덧붙여 표시된 의미입니다.

senses.en: To signify beyond its literal or principal meaning.

examples.text: The word "hearth" often connotes coziness and warmth.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 connotō('덧붙여 표시하다')에서 왔습니다. 글자 뜻 너머를 함께 가리킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by extreme care and great effort

examples.text: A conscientious editor, she checked every citation twice before the book went to print.

senses.en: guided by or in accordance with conscience or sense of right and wrong

examples.text: As a conscientious objector, he refused to take part in the war on moral grounds.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 cōnscientiōsus에서 왔고 conscience(양심)와 같은 계통입니다. 양심에 비추어 꼼꼼하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: render holy by means of religious rites

examples.text: The bishop consecrated the new cathedral in a ceremony attended by thousands.

senses.en: give entirely to a specific person, activity, or cause

examples.text: She consecrated her career to the cause of public health reform.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnsecrāre에서 왔고 중세 영어 consecraten으로 들어왔습니다. 제단과 교회를 신께 바친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: agreement in the judgment or opinion reached by a group as a whole

examples.text: There is a growing scientific consensus that the underlying cause is environmental rather than genetic.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnsēnsus('일치, 합의')에서 왔고, cōnsentiō(함께 느끼다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: a schoolhouse with special facilities for fine arts

examples.text: She trained at a famous conservatory before joining the national symphony orchestra.

senses.en: a greenhouse in which plants are arranged in a pleasing manner

examples.text: Tropical orchids bloomed year-round in the glass conservatory behind the manor.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 cōnservātōrium에서 왔고, cōnservāre(보존하다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 재능을 보존해 가르치는 곳입니다.

senses.en: think about carefully; weigh

examples.text: The board will consider several proposals before choosing a new director.

senses.en: show consideration for; take into account

examples.text: The judge considered the defendant's youth when deciding on a sentence.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 considerer와 라틴어 considerare를 거쳐 중세 영어에 들어온 말입니다.

senses.en: give moral or emotional strength to

examples.text: Friends tried to console her after the failure of her business.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 consoler와 라틴어 cōnsōlor('위로하다')에서 왔고, solace(위안)와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: make firm or secure; strengthen

examples.text: The new government moved quickly to consolidate its power after the election.

senses.en: bring together into a single whole or system

examples.text: The town and county schools are being consolidated

origin.ko: 라틴어 consolidō에서 왔고, solidus(단단한)에서 갈라졌습니다. 흩어진 것을 한데 단단히 굳힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: obvious to the eye or mind

examples.text: He was conspicuous by his absence.

senses.en: without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious

examples.text: The mayor showed conspicuous disregard for the rules he had himself written.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conspicuus('눈에 보이는, 두드러진')에서 왔고, cōnspicere(알아채다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: engage in plotting or enter into a conspiracy, swear together

examples.text: They conspired to overthrow the government

senses.en: To work together to bring about.

examples.text: Rain and sweat conspired to smudge her mascara.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conspīrō('함께 숨쉬다')에서 왔습니다. 숨결을 맞춰 몰래 뜻을 합친다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: steadfast in purpose or devotion or affection

examples.text: He remained a constant friend through every hardship in her long career.

senses.en: unvarying in nature

examples.text: maintained a constant temperature

origin.ko: 라틴어 constans에서 왔고 cōnstāre('굳건히 서다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 흔들리지 않고 선다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the body of voters who elect a representative for their area

examples.text: The senator spent the recess meeting with members of her constituency across the rural counties.

origin.ko: constituent(구성하는 사람)에 -ency가 붙은 말입니다. 대표를 함께 세우는 유권자 집단입니다.

senses.en: an abstract part of something

examples.text: Hydrogen and oxygen are the constituents of water.

senses.en: a member of a constituency; a citizen who is represented in a government by officials for whom he or she votes

examples.text: The congresswoman answered letters from constituents worried about rising healthcare costs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnstituēns에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 statuō(세우다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 함께 세워 이루는 부분입니다.

senses.en: form or compose

examples.text: Women constitute a majority of the students enrolled in the program.

senses.en: set up or lay the groundwork for

examples.text: The assembly was constituted to draft a new charter for the republic.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnstituō('세우다, 확립하다')에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 statuō(세우다)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: lacking spontaneity; not natural

examples.text: a constrained smile

senses.en: Forced; compelled.

examples.text: Constrained by a tight budget, the committee had to cancel several planned events.

senses.en: Something that constrains; a restriction.

examples.text: Budget constraints forced the museum to postpone its planned expansion.

senses.en: The repression of one's feelings.

examples.text: There was a noticeable constraint between the two old friends after their quarrel.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 constreinte(constreindre의 과거분사)에서 왔고, 라틴어 cōnstringō(묶다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: squeeze or press together

examples.text: Cold temperatures cause blood vessels near the skin to constrict.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnstrictus('압축된')에서 왔고, cōnstringō(함께 묶다, 조이다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: make sense of; assign a meaning to

examples.text: Her silence was construed as agreement, though she had merely been thinking.

origin.ko: 라틴어 construo('함께 쌓다')에서 왔고, 후기 라틴어에서 '문법적으로 엮다'는 뜻이 되었습니다. construct와 같은 어원입니다.

senses.en: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill

examples.text: a consummate artist

senses.en: make perfect; bring to perfection

examples.text: The treaty consummated years of delicate negotiation between the two rival nations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnsummātus('다 합쳐 완성한')에서 왔고, summa(합계)에서 갈라졌습니다. 모든 것을 더해 끝까지 완성했다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike

examples.text: She regarded the empty promises of politicians with open contempt.

senses.en: a willful disobedience to or disrespect for the authority of a court or legislative body

examples.text: The witness was held in contempt of court after repeatedly refusing to answer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contemptus('경멸')에서 왔고, contemnō(경멸하다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: expressing extreme contempt

examples.text: Sir George burst into a loud fit of contemptuous laughter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contemptus(경멸)에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: maintain or assert

examples.text: He contended that Communism had no future

senses.en: compete for something; engage in a contest; measure oneself against others

examples.text: Three teams are contending for the championship this season.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contendere('팽팽히 뻗다, 애쓰다')에서 왔습니다. 서로 팔을 뻗어 겨룬다는 뜻에서 '주장하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: inclined or showing an inclination to dispute or disagree, even to engage in law suits

examples.text: His contentious temperament turned every committee meeting into a prolonged argument.

senses.en: involving or likely to cause controversy

examples.text: The council voted on a contentious proposal to rezone the historic waterfront.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contentiōsus('다투기 좋아하는')에서 왔고, contendere(겨루다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: To place something or someone in a particular context.

examples.text: The curator added panels to contextualize the artifacts within the broader history of the region.

senses.en: being determined by conditions or circumstances that follow

examples.text: arms sales contingent on the approval of Congress

senses.en: possible but not certain to occur

examples.text: The firm set aside funds for contingent expenses that might arise during construction.

senses.en: a gathering of persons representative of some larger group

examples.text: each nation sent a contingent of athletes to the Olympics

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 contingens('가능한, 우연한')에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 tangere(닿다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 조건에 맞닿아야 일어난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: become smaller or draw together

examples.text: Metal contracts as it cools, which is why bridges include expansion gaps.

senses.en: be stricken by an illness, fall victim to an illness

examples.text: Several of the sailors contracted malaria during the long voyage.

senses.en: a binding agreement between two or more persons that is enforceable by law

examples.text: Both parties signed the contract, which specified penalties for late delivery.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contrahere('함께 끌어당기다')에서 왔습니다. 동사는 원래 '오그라들다'였고, 계약 뜻은 나중에 생겼습니다.

senses.en: resistant to guidance or discipline

examples.text: The contrary child refused every suggestion simply because it came from an adult.

senses.en: very opposed in nature or character or purpose

examples.text: the facts point to a contrary conclusion

origin.ko: 라틴어 contrārius('반대의')에서 왔고 contrā(~에 맞서)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: go against, as of rules and laws

examples.text: The company's dumping of waste contravenes several environmental regulations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contraveniō('맞서 오다')에서 온 중세 프랑스어 contravenir에서 왔습니다. 규칙과 정면으로 부딪친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an awkward clash

examples.text: A minor contretemps over seating arrangements delayed the start of the state dinner.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 contretemps를 그대로 빌려 온 말입니다.

senses.en: feeling or expressing pain or sorrow for sins or offenses

examples.text: The contrite executive issued a public apology and promised to repay the lost funds.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contrītus('산산이 갈린')에서 왔고 conterō(갈다, 짓이기다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 마음이 부서지도록 뉘우친다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: The state of being contrite; sincere penitence or remorse.

examples.text: Kremlin officials have shown no signs of contrition.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 contriciun에서 왔고 라틴어 contrītiō가 뿌리입니다. contrite와 같은 계통으로 마음이 부서지는 뉘우침입니다.

senses.en: come up with (an idea, plan, explanation, theory, or principle) after a mental effort

examples.text: The engineers contrived a clever system for recycling water on the remote research station.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 controver에서 왔고 trover('찾다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 방법을 찾아내 고안한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Unnatural, forced; artificial, or unrealistic.

examples.text: Critics found the plot contrived, with coincidences piling up to force a happy ending.

senses.en: wilfully obstinate; stubbornly disobedient

examples.text: The contumacious witness ignored the court's summons for the third time.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contumāx('고집 센, 완강한')에 -ious가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: an injury that doesn't break the skin but results in some discoloration

examples.text: The fall left a large contusion on his thigh but no broken bones.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 contusion에서 왔고, 라틴어 contundō('두들기다')가 뿌리입니다. 세게 두들겨 생긴 멍입니다.

senses.en: a difficult problem

examples.text: How to expand access without raising costs remains the central conundrum of the reform.

origin.ko: 기원 불명의 말로, 스콜라 철학식 라틴어를 흉내 낸 장난스러운 신조어에서 인기를 얻었습니다.

senses.en: get over an illness or shock

examples.text: The patient convalesced for six months after his stroke.

origin.ko: 라틴어 convalēscere에서 왔고, valēscere('강해지기 시작하다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 다시 튼튼해지는 과정입니다.

senses.en: returning to health after illness or debility

examples.text: She stayed in a convalescent hospital for two weeks before returning home.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 convalescent에서 왔고 라틴어 convalēscere('강해지기 시작하다')가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: A practice or procedure widely observed in a group, especially to facilitate social interaction; a custom.

examples.text: The convention of driving on the right is reinforced by law.

senses.en: a large formal assembly

examples.text: Delegates from every state gathered at the party's national convention to choose a nominee.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conventiō('모임, 합의')에서 왔고, conveniō(함께 모이다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 모여서 합의한 것이 '관습'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: unimaginative and conformist

examples.text: The film's conventional plot offered few surprises to seasoned viewers.

senses.en: following accepted customs and proprieties

examples.text: conventional wisdom

senses.en: move or draw together at a certain location

examples.text: The crowd converged on the movie star

origin.ko: 라틴어 convergere에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 vergere(기울다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 한 점을 향해 함께 기운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (usually followed by ‘with’) well informed about or knowing thoroughly

examples.text: She is equally conversant with Shakespeare and the laws of physics.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 conversant(converser의 현재분사)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: with the terms of the relation reversed

examples.text: Higher taxes can reduce spending; conversely, tax cuts often stimulate it.

senses.en: an unshakable belief in something without need for proof or evidence

examples.text: She spoke with such conviction that even skeptics in the audience began to nod.

senses.en: (criminal law) a final judgment of guilty in a criminal case and the punishment that is imposed

examples.text: the conviction came as no surprise

origin.ko: 라틴어 convictiō에서 왔고, convincō(설득하다, 유죄를 입증하다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 논쟁에서 완전히 이긴 확신입니다.

senses.en: make (someone) agree, understand, or realize the truth or validity of something

examples.text: He convinced me I had talent, and persuaded me to study music.

origin.ko: 라틴어 convincō('논박하다, 입증하다')에서 왔고, con-과 vincō(정복하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 논리로 완전히 이겨 납득시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: occupied with or fond of the pleasures of good company

examples.text: a woman of convivial nature

origin.ko: 라틴어 convīvium('잔치')에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 vīvō(살다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 함께 먹고 사는 즐거움입니다.

senses.en: call together

examples.text: The president convoked an emergency session of the council to discuss the crisis.

origin.ko: 라틴어 convocare에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 vocō(부르다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 사람들을 한데 불러 모은다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: highly complex or intricate and occasionally devious

examples.text: He gave a convoluted explanation that amounted to little more than a weak excuse for his absence.

senses.en: large in number or quantity (especially of discourse)

examples.text: she took copious notes

origin.ko: 라틴어 copiosus에서 왔고, copia('풍부함')가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: diffusing warmth and friendliness

examples.text: Since then, though, discussions have become more collaborative and cordial.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 cordiālis('심장의')에서 왔습니다. 마음에서 우러난 따뜻함입니다.

senses.en: the property of being extremely abundant

examples.text: The open-air market offered a cornucopia of fruits, spices, and handmade crafts.

senses.en: a goat's horn filled with grain and flowers and fruit symbolizing prosperity

examples.text: The harvest festival poster showed a cornucopia spilling over with grapes and wheat.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cornūcōpia('풍요의 뿔')를 빌려 온 말입니다. 과일과 곡식이 쏟아지는 뿔 모양 장식입니다.

senses.en: a practical consequence that follows naturally

examples.text: blind jealousy is a frequent corollary of passionate love

senses.en: (logic) an inference that follows directly from the proof of another proposition

examples.text: The second theorem has an immediate corollary that every such set is finite.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 corōllārium('화환 값, 덤')에서 왔고, corōlla(작은 화관)가 뿌리입니다. 덤으로 따라오는 결론이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having material or physical form or substance

examples.text: The ghost in the story had no corporeal form and passed easily through walls.

senses.en: affecting or characteristic of the body as opposed to the mind or spirit

examples.text: The monk renounced corporeal pleasures in pursuit of spiritual discipline.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 corporealle에서 왔고, 라틴어 corporeus와 corpus(몸)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: excessively fat

examples.text: The corpulent innkeeper wheezed as he climbed the narrow stairs with our luggage.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 corpulent를 거친 라틴어 corpulentus(몸집이 큰)에서 왔습니다. corpus(몸)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: to bear a reciprocal or mutual relation

examples.text: Doctrine and worship correlate as theory and practice.

origin.ko: cor-(함께)에 relate(관련짓다)가 붙은 말입니다. 서로를 함께 연결해 가져온다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: establish or strengthen as with new evidence or facts

examples.text: Two independent witnesses corroborated her account of what happened that night.

origin.ko: 라틴어 corrōborō('강하게 하다')에서 왔고, con-과 rōbur(힘)가 합쳐졌습니다. 증거를 더해 힘을 실어 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: composed of people from or at home in many parts of the world; especially not provincial in attitudes or interests

examples.text: Lisbon has grown into a cosmopolitan city, home to residents from dozens of countries.

senses.en: growing or occurring in many parts of the world

examples.text: a cosmopolitan herb

origin.ko: cosmopolite(세계 시민)에 -an이 붙은 말입니다. metropolitan(대도시의)과 비교됩니다.

senses.en: treat with excessive indulgence

examples.text: The car cossets its occupants in comfort.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cotsǣta('오두막 사는 사람')에서 왔을 것으로 추정되며, 확실하지는 않습니다.

senses.en: an exclusive circle of people with a common purpose

examples.text: A tightly knit coterie of executive powerbrokers made all the real decisions in the company.

senses.en: being of equal extent or scope or duration

examples.text: The county's borders are coterminous with those of the old medieval parish.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conterminus에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 terminus(경계)가 합쳐졌습니다. 경계를 함께 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: consent to, give permission; permit

examples.text: The university will not countenance any form of plagiarism among its students.

senses.en: the appearance conveyed by a person's face

examples.text: Her calm countenance gave no hint of the anxiety she felt before the verdict.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 countenance에서 왔고, contenir(함께 지니다)와 후기 라틴어 continentia에서 갈라졌습니다. 표정을 받아들이듯 허용한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: contrary to what common sense would suggest

examples.text: It seems counterintuitive, but resting after a mild injury can slow recovery more than gentle exercise.

origin.ko: counter-와 intuitive를 합친 말로, 1955년 노엄 촘스키가 처음 만들어 썼습니다.

senses.en: cancel officially

examples.text: The general countermanded the order to advance after learning of the approaching storm.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 contramandō에서 왔습니다. 앞선 명령에 '반대되는 명령'을 내리니 '취소하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Any similar contrasting element in a work of art.

examples.text: The comic scenes serve as a counterpoint to the play's otherwise grim tone.

senses.en: a musical form involving the simultaneous sound of two or more melodies

examples.text: Bach's mastery of counterpoint allows several independent melodies to weave together seamlessly.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 contrāpūnctum에서 왔습니다. 음표(점) 맞은편에 다른 음표를 대응시킨다는 데서 '대조 요소'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: tending to hinder the achievement of a goal

examples.text: Punishing students for asking questions is counterproductive and discourages genuine curiosity.

senses.en: seek someone's favor

examples.text: The candidate spent the summer courting wealthy donors in several cities.

senses.en: an assembly (including one or more judges) to conduct judicial business

examples.text: The appeals court overturned the earlier ruling on procedural grounds.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cohors(울타리 친 뜰)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 궁정에서 군주의 환심을 사려 한 데서 '구애하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: secret or hidden; not openly practiced or engaged in or shown or avowed

examples.text: covert operations

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 covert(덮인)에서 왔고 cover의 과거분사입니다. 덮여 있어 '은밀한' 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: wish, long, or crave for (something, especially the property of another person)

examples.text: Rival museums coveted the rare manuscript and made repeated offers to its owner.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 covoitier(욕망)에서 왔으며 라틴어 cupiditas(강한 욕망)와 관련됩니다.

senses.en: subdue, restrain, or overcome by affecting with a feeling of awe; frighten (as with threats)

examples.text: Con artists are not cowed by the law.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 kúga(억압하다)에서 왔을 것으로 추정됩니다.

senses.en: To crouch or cringe, or to avoid or shy away from something, in fear.

examples.text: The villagers cowered in their cellars while the storm tore roofs from the houses.

origin.ko: 중세 저지 독일어 kûren(웅크리고 숨어 기다리다) 등에서 왔다고 봅니다. 몸을 구부린 자세가 '움츠러들다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: showing marked and often playful or irritating evasiveness or reluctance to make a definite or committing statement

examples.text: a politician coy about his intentions

senses.en: affectedly modest or shy especially in a playful or provocative way

examples.text: She gave a coy smile and refused to reveal who had sent the flowers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 quiētus(조용한, 쉬는)에서 고대 프랑스어 coi를 거쳐 왔습니다. 조용히 빼는 태도에서 '내숭 떠는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: cheat or trick

examples.text: The charlatan cozened the widow out of her life savings with promises of a miracle cure.
